reason: Bearer-token authentication on /mcp had no abuse limit, unlike the website's login. The product now answers 429 after repeated failed token attempts from one address (same in-process pattern as the auth limiter: 10 failures per 15 minutes) and after too many requests per token (300 per minute). The spec has no step for either.

changes.after: (Run this step LAST in a pass: it locks the tester's address out of /mcp for 15 minutes.) Run 11 times: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} " -H "Authorization: Bearer sbpat_not-a-real-token" -X POST <API_BASE>/mcp`. Expect ten responses of `401` followed by `429`. Then run `curl -s -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sbpat_not-a-real-token" -X POST <API_BASE>/mcp`. Expect status 429, a `Retry-After` header of at most 900, and a JSON body whose `error.data.code` is `rate_limited`.
changes.tracesTo: docs/changes/platform-mcp.md 'Known limitations' (Rate limiting of /mcp is not added in this version); server/routes/auth.js authLimiter (10 attempts / 15 min / IP)
changes.reason: A guessed-token flood must be slowed the same way a password-guessing flood is.
